importantNotes: Ezekiel's vision of God's throne (ch. 1) is one of the most complex visions in Scripture.
The departure of God's glory from the Temple (chs. 10-11) is a devastating moment.
'I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit in you' (36:26) — the promise of inner transformation.
The Valley of Dry Bones (ch. 37) represents Israel's national resurrection.
Chapters 40-48 describe a future Temple — debated whether literal or symbolic.

chapters.1: Ezekiel's vision of the glory of God — the four living creatures and the wheel within a wheel.
chapters.2: God commissions Ezekiel as a prophet to rebellious Israel.
chapters.3: Ezekiel eats the scroll; he is appointed as a watchman for Israel.
chapters.4: Ezekiel acts out the siege of Jerusalem using a clay model.
chapters.5: Ezekiel shaves his head — a sign of Jerusalem's coming destruction.
chapters.6: Prophecy against the mountains of Israel — judgment on idolatry.
chapters.7: The end has come — judgment on the land of Israel is imminent.
chapters.8: Ezekiel is shown the abominations being committed in the Temple in Jerusalem.
chapters.9: Those who grieve over sin are marked; the rest are slain by angelic executioners.
chapters.10: The glory of the LORD begins to depart from the Temple.
chapters.11: Judgment on corrupt leaders; God's glory leaves the Temple; promise of restoration.
chapters.12: Ezekiel acts out the exile — packing his bags through a hole in the wall.
chapters.13: Condemnation of false prophets and prophetesses who deceive the people.
chapters.14: Idolaters will receive God's judgment; even Noah, Daniel, and Job could only save themselves.
chapters.15: Jerusalem is like a useless vine — fit only for burning.
chapters.16: An allegory of unfaithful Jerusalem — rescued by God, then unfaithful despite His love.
chapters.17: The parable of two eagles and a vine — Babylon, Egypt, and Judah's broken covenant.
chapters.18: Individual responsibility — 'the soul who sins shall die'; God takes no pleasure in death.
chapters.19: A lament for the princes of Israel — lions captured and vines uprooted.
chapters.20: God recounts Israel's history of rebellion from Egypt to the present.
chapters.21: The sword of the LORD is drawn; judgment falls on Jerusalem and Ammon.
chapters.22: Jerusalem's sins listed — bloodshed, idolatry, injustice; no intercessor found.
chapters.23: The allegory of Oholah (Samaria) and Oholibah (Jerusalem) — unfaithful sisters.
chapters.24: The parable of the cooking pot; Ezekiel's wife dies — he is not allowed to mourn.
chapters.25: Oracles against Ammon, Moab, Edom, and Philistia.
chapters.26: Oracle against Tyre — the great city will be destroyed.
chapters.27: A lament over Tyre — once a magnificent trading ship, now sunk.
chapters.28: Judgment on the king of Tyre (with echoes of Satan's fall); oracle against Sidon.
chapters.29: Oracle against Egypt — Pharaoh is like a great river monster.
chapters.30: Egypt's allies will fall; God will use Babylon to judge Egypt.
chapters.31: Egypt compared to a great cedar tree that will be cut down.
chapters.32: A lament over Pharaoh; Egypt descends to the realm of the dead.
chapters.33: Ezekiel is again appointed watchman; Jerusalem has fallen — a turning point.
chapters.34: God condemns Israel's false shepherds; He Himself will shepherd His flock.
chapters.35: Judgment on Mount Seir (Edom) for its hatred of Israel.
chapters.36: Prophecy to the mountains of Israel — restoration; 'I will give you a new heart.'
chapters.37: The Valley of Dry Bones — God will resurrect and reunite Israel; one nation, one king.
chapters.38: Prophecy against Gog from the land of Magog — a future invasion of Israel.
chapters.39: God defeats Gog; Israel buries the dead for seven months; God's glory revealed.
chapters.40: Ezekiel's vision of the future Temple — detailed measurements of the outer courts.
chapters.41: Measurements of the inner Temple sanctuary.
chapters.42: The priests' chambers and the sacred areas of the Temple.
chapters.43: The glory of the LORD returns to fill the new Temple.
chapters.44: Regulations for the east gate, the Levites, and the Zadokite priests.
chapters.45: The sacred district and the prince's responsibilities; offerings and festivals.
chapters.46: Regulations for worship, the prince's offerings, and the kitchen courts.
chapters.47: The river of life flowing from the Temple — bringing life wherever it goes.
chapters.48: The division of the land among the twelve tribes; the city's name: 'The LORD is There.'
